summary: Updates RFC 4055 with new conventions for the parameters of the RSAES-OAEP and RSASSA-PSS algorithms in X.509 certificates. It clarifies how parameters should be encoded. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Some locks need small settings written on them. This update fixes the way those settings are written down in certificates, so everyone reads them the same way.

subtitle: A small fix to how RSA-OAEP and RSA-PSS parameters appear in X.509 certificates.

tldr.problem: RFC 4055 let RSAES-OAEP parameters appear in a certificate's public key field and described RSASSA-PSS parameter placement unclearly, even using the wrong field name.
tldr.mechanism: This document replaces specific paragraphs of RFC 4055. RSAES-OAEP parameters MUST be absent in subjectPublicKeyInfo, and RSASSA-PSS-params placement is spelled out for certificates and CRLs.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 4055 in a narrow way, and the authors say implementers had no objections because current implementations were not affected.

facts.label: PSS params in CA public key

today: RFC 5756 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 4055, and the unit data lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Read it together with RFC 4055.

sections.title: What This Update Changes
sections.content:
RFC 4055 describes how to use the RSA Encryption Scheme with Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding (RSAES-OAEP) in the Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure. This document updates RFC 4055 and only touches two paragraphs about RSAES-OAEP parameters in certificates: the second paragraph of its Section 4 and the first paragraph of its Section 4.1. It also fixes incorrect references to a publicKeyAlgorithms field and rewords the second and third paragraphs of RFC 4055 Section 3 for clarity.

The change is motivated by the PKIX Elliptic Curve Cryptography design team's recommendation that Key Derivation Functions (KDFs) should not be constrained within a certificate. Constraints on KDFs should instead be negotiated in the protocols that use certificates. Each change is shown as an Old: block followed by a New: block.
sections.eli5: This note fixes a few sentences in an older rulebook. It shows the old words and then the new words.

sections.title: RSASSA-PSS Parameter Placement
sections.content:
The first change clarifies where RSASSA-PSS-params go in the signature, signatureAlgorithm and subjectPublicKeyInfo fields of certification authority (CA) and end-entity (EE) certificates, and in the signatureAlgorithm field of certificate revocation lists (CRLs). The new text says:

  • When id-RSASSA-PSS appears in the signature algorithm field of a TBSCertificate or TBSCertList, the RSASSA-PSS-params structure MUST be included in the signature parameters field.
  • In the subjectPublicKeyInfo algorithm field of CA certificates, the parameters field SHOULD include RSASSA-PSS-params. In EE certificates it MAY.
  • All certificates and CRLs signed by a CA that supports id-RSASSA-PSS MUST include RSASSA-PSS-params in the signatureAlgorithm parameters.
sections.eli5: If a certificate is signed with this method, the signing settings must be written next to the signature. On the key itself they are suggested for certificate authorities and optional for everyone else.

sections.title: No RSAES-OAEP Parameters in Public Keys
sections.content:
The second change prohibits putting RSAES-OAEP-params in the subjectPublicKeyInfo field. CAs that issue certificates with the id-RSAES-OAEP algorithm identifier MUST NOT include parameters in the subjectPublicKeyInfo algorithm field. The old text had a SHOULD requiring parameters, and told entities what defaults to use when they were absent.

The RFC gives two reasons: it does not affect interoperability, and it matches the PKIX practice of not placing limits on how a public key can be used in subjectPublicKeyInfo. A poll of implementers raised no objections because current implementations were not affected.
sections.eli5: The label on the public key should not say how the key may be used. Those details belong somewhere else.

sections.title: The Algorithm Identifier Rule
sections.content: The third change rewrites the first paragraph of RFC 4055 Section 4.1 with the same reasoning. Whenever id-RSAES-OAEP is used in an AlgorithmIdentifier, the parameters MUST employ the RSAES-OAEP-params syntax. The old text said the parameters may be absent or present as subject public key information. Now they MUST be absent when used in the subjectPublicKeyInfo field, and they MUST still be present when used in the algorithm identifier associated with an encrypted value.
sections.eli5: On a public key label the settings are left out. On an actual locked message the settings must be included.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The security considerations of RFC 4055 still apply. In addition, if the RSAES-OAEP-params are negotiated, the negotiation mechanism needs to provide integrity for them. For example, an S/MIME agent can advertise its capabilities in the SMIMECapabilities attribute, which is either a signed attribute or a certificate extension.
sections.eli5: If two sides agree on settings, nobody must be able to quietly change what they agreed on.
